title: Compiler Errors and Warnings
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of compiler errors and warnings using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates compiler errors and warnings.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Compiler Errors and Warnings** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Apply compiler errors and warnings by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Reading Error Messages, Understanding Type Errors, Using Warnings to Improve Code—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

items.title: Reading Error Messages
items.text: Reading Error Messages helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: Understanding Type Errors
items.text: Understanding Type Errors is one part of compiler errors and warnings. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Catching every exception and ignoring it is a safe recovery strategy.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
